title: API Security Engineering
centralQuestion: How does the API remain trustworthy when callers, credentials, inputs, destinations, dependencies, and networks cannot be trusted by default?
responsibility: Derive, implement, and adversarially verify security properties around the durable service without replacing engineering judgment with middleware or scanner output.
incomingBoundary: The Course 2 API 1.2 durable-service handoff and migrations 001–005.
outgoingBoundary: Security Profile 1.0, migrations 006–007, a threat-to-requirement security case, identity and authorization policy, hostile-input vectors, SSRF and webhook protections, abuse controls, and incident evidence.
versionState: API 1.2 preserved; Security Profile 1.0 introduced; migrations 001–007.
languageStrategy: one primary implementation track plus one comparative reference track

modules.title: Threat Modeling and Security Requirements
modules.centralQuestion: Which assets, actors, trust boundaries, abuse cases, and assumptions define the real security problem?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Create a security case that traces threats to requirements, control owners, tests, and residual risk.
learningOutcomes: Identify assets, actors, entry points, and trust boundaries
Write concrete abuse cases and security invariants
Use STRIDE as a prompt rather than a substitute for analysis
Rank risk with explicit assumptions
Trace every control to a threat, requirement, owner, and test

modules.title: HTTP Edge and Canonicalization
modules.centralQuestion: Which raw HTTP message should the application trust after proxies, parsers, duplicate fields, and size limits intervene?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Establish host, forwarding, media-type, strict-JSON, body-size, and canonicalization rules before model validation.
learningOutcomes: Define direct-client and trusted-proxy behavior
Reject ambiguous singleton headers and duplicate JSON members
Normalize only after preserving raw evidence
Enforce content type and body limits before model validation
Separate browser CORS policy from API authentication

modules.title: Authentication and Token Validation
modules.centralQuestion: How should a resource server validate bearer tokens and API keys without trusting convenient claims?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Implement issuer, audience, algorithm, key, lifetime, revocation, subject, tenant, and scope validation.
learningOutcomes: Accept exactly one credential mechanism
Select accepted JWT algorithms from server configuration
Validate signature, type, issuer, audience, time, subject, tenant, scopes, and token ID
Handle key rotation and unknown key identifiers safely
Store API-key digests rather than reusable keys

modules.title: Authorization and Policy Enforcement
modules.centralQuestion: How are scopes, roles, ownership, tenant membership, relationships, assurance, and freshness combined under default deny?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Build explicit authorization decisions for collections, individual resources, fields, support access, and administration.
learningOutcomes: Separate authentication from authorization
Model operation policy explicitly
Constrain collection queries before loading data
Apply field-level input and output policy
Prevent existence leaks and stale authorization decisions

modules.title: Hostile Input and File Handling
modules.centralQuestion: How are hostile strings, numbers, paths, filenames, uploads, and serialized structures constrained at the correct boundary?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Harden input parsing, Unicode, traversal, MIME, streaming upload, checksum, query, and error behavior.
learningOutcomes: Distinguish schema validation from semantic security validation
Reject traversal after decoding and normalization
Treat filenames as labels, never paths
Bound archive and upload expansion
Prevent SQL, command, template, and deserialization injection

modules.title: Outbound HTTP, SSRF, and Webhook Integrity
modules.centralQuestion: How can outbound HTTP and webhook delivery avoid SSRF, rebinding, redirect abuse, tampering, and replay?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Implement destination policy, address classification, peer verification, exact-byte signatures, freshness, rotation, and replay defense.
learningOutcomes: Reject forbidden schemes, ports, credentials, fragments, and address ranges
Evaluate every resolved address and the connected peer
Revalidate redirects and DNS changes
Sign exact webhook bytes with key identity and timestamp
Reject stale and replayed deliveries

modules.title: Secrets, Cryptography, and Sensitive Data
modules.centralQuestion: How should secrets, cryptographic keys, sensitive fields, logs, retention, and audit evidence be handled?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Add secret-provider boundaries, non-rendering values, redaction, pseudonymization, rotation, and privacy-bounded audit records.
learningOutcomes: Distinguish hashing, HMAC, encryption, and password hashing
Keep secret values out of representation and logs
Rotate signing and verification keys with overlap
Redact nested structures and embedded credentials
Minimize, retain, and delete sensitive data deliberately

modules.title: Abuse Resistance and Resource Budgets
modules.centralQuestion: How can the service resist brute force and resource exhaustion without turning traffic control into false authorization?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Introduce principal/tenant/operation/cost budgets, concurrency permits, quotas, and bounded degradation.
learningOutcomes: Choose rate-limit dimensions from abuse paths
Implement deterministic token-bucket behavior
Limit simultaneous expensive work with leak-free permits
Bound uploads, streams, queue depth, and storage
Return coherent `429` or `503` outcomes without amplifying retries

modules.title: Adversarial Verification and Supply-Chain Assurance
modules.centralQuestion: How do adversarial tests and supply-chain evidence show that controls fail closed and that the proof is sensitive?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Build hostile vectors, negative policy tests, planted vulnerabilities, dependency evidence, SBOM/provenance routes, and scanner disposition.
learningOutcomes: Trace tests to threats and requirements
Remove or mutate controls and confirm the proof fails
Use shared hostile vectors across languages
Pin direct and transitive dependencies and produce an SBOM
Interpret scanner output instead of treating tools as authorities

modules.title: Security Operations and Incident Response
modules.centralQuestion: How is a suspected compromise detected, contained, investigated, rotated, patched, and converted into improved requirements?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Run a controlled credential and cross-tenant incident with timelines, revocation, rotation, release, and threat-model revision.
learningOutcomes: Design actionable security events and audit records
Revoke tokens and API keys deliberately
Rotate webhook and signing keys with overlap
Preserve timelines and confidence levels
Update threats, controls, and tests after the incident
